key_insight: EHR representations entangle physiology with care processes, and neither value-versus-ordering decomposition nor cross-site outcome invariance alone identifies the biological component.
clinical_relevance: Cross-site differences in model behavior may reflect testing practices, case mix, or information loss rather than a change in underlying biology.
method: Formalized physiology, test ordering, recorded values, representations, and clinical environments.
Used information-theoretic analysis and observationally equivalent models to establish identification limits.
Derived conditions under which universally measured or sufficiently informative tests restore identification.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents theoretical results and a worked example showing a 9.6-percentage-point cross-site gap despite an unchanged biological mechanism, rather than clinical validation.
watch_item: Report cross-site invariance analyses as tests of a stated joint hypothesis; passing or failing them alone does not establish biological invariance.
paper_title: The Dark Matter of Clinical Data: An Identification Limit on Disentangling Physiology from Care Process in electronic health records
